As someone who grew up in China, I honestly don’t have very high expectations for Chinese restaurants in NYC. They almost always feel commercial to me—but not necessarily “commercially” good, even when they have excellent reviews.

We were strolling around SoHo and chose this place for dinner almost randomly. Even before walking in, I saw two large groups of non-Chinese diners waiting by the entrance and thought to myself, another place that’s probably just going to be OK.

I couldn’t have been more wrong.

Except for the fact that the staff members we encountered spoke fluent English, everything else somehow felt so… Chinese.

The service was friendly in exactly the right amount. No one kept coming over to ask, as a formality, whether “everything was good.” At one point, I switched one dish for another, half “admitting” that I wanted to learn some tricks from that particular dish, and the waitress simply gave me this genuine, understanding smile.

Later, all of our dishes had arrived except one, and we weren’t quite sure whether it had actually been included in our order. When we asked another waitress, she immediately understood what we meant and responded in such a calm, reassuring way—without treating the question as if we were pushing her to hurry up with the dish.

There’s a nuanced difference there, if you know what I mean.

The food also came out unexpectedly fast, and the flavors were spot-on. That, of course, is the biggest reason I came away thinking: this place is authentic.

And then there was the space itself.

When we were first seated, I felt lucky that the two of us had been given a four-person table. But once I sat down and looked around, I realized they simply weren’t “stingy” with their seating arrangements. That kind of generosity with space is not particularly common in NYC restaurants.

At first, I also thought the room was a little noisy and perhaps not very conducive to a deep conversation. Half an hour later, though, we found ourselves talking about our feelings toward different family members. Somehow, the ambience was just right: enough life and noise around us that you could let some emotion out, without the room becoming so quiet that you suddenly felt exposed and responsible for filling every silence.

When we walked out, I said to myself, I really need to leave a positive review for this team.

5ive Spice Tacos & Banh Mi on Mulberry Street is an interesting alternative to the Italian restaurants nearby. The menu draws from Vietnamese cooking, with a particular emphasis on pho, banh mi and a creative interpretation of Vietnamese crispy pancakes.

The banh xeo tacos are one of the restaurant's most distinctive ideas. Traditional banh xeo is a crispy Vietnamese pancake made with rice flour and coconut milk. Using that style of preparation as a taco shell creates a contrast between the delicate, crisp exterior and the savoury filling.

Pho is another important part of the menu. The broth is the foundation of the dish, developed through aromatic ingredients and long cooking. Rice noodles, herbs, meat and fresh garnishes allow diners to adjust the balance of flavours.

The banh mi sandwiches offer a more portable alternative. A good banh mi depends on the contrast between crisp bread, savoury fillings, pickled vegetables and fresh herbs. The acidity of the vegetables is particularly important because it balances the richer ingredients.

The restaurant has a casual atmosphere and is better suited to an informal lunch or dinner than a special-occasion meal. The dining room is relatively straightforward, with the emphasis on food rather than elaborate decoration.

One advantage is the variety of formats available. Diners can choose a substantial bowl of soup, a sandwich or smaller dishes depending on their appetite.

5ive Spice is particularly interesting because it brings recognizable Vietnamese ingredients into slightly different combinations while maintaining the freshness and contrasting textures associated with Vietnamese cooking.
Great flavors, great service.

I’ve been coming to this ramen place since 2019, and it honestly hurts to leave a review like this because I genuinely loved this place. However, today was the last straw.

I ordered the Tontoro Pork Ramen, and once again, the meat itself was cold. This isn’t the first time this has happened, which makes the experience even more disappointing. For a restaurant that serves ramen, the food should be prepared properly and served at the right temperature.

What made the experience worse was how the staff handled my concern. The staff members I interacted with were Spanish-speaking, and I felt like I was being looked at judgmentally when I tried to address the issue. I asked a simple question about whether the meat was always cooked properly, and instead of giving me an explanation or addressing my concern, they looked at me carelessly and completely ignored my question. I found the whole interaction disrespectful and unprofessional.

I honestly don’t know why I was treated that way. I even wondered whether my being Asian had anything to do with it. I’m not going to make accusations without knowing for sure, but the way I was looked at and dismissed left me feeling uncomfortable and questioning the interaction.

The food quality was already disappointing, but the lack of basic communication and customer service made it worse. I wasn’t asking for anything unreasonable. I just wanted my food prepared properly and my concerns taken seriously.

It’s genuinely disappointing when a place you’ve enjoyed and supported since 2019 gives you a reason to stop coming back. I really loved this restaurant, which is why this experience was so frustrating. Unfortunately, after repeated issues with the food and the way my concerns were handled, I won’t be returning.

You can lose a loyal customer over repeated problems, but making them feel unwelcome when they raise a legitimate concern is what finally pushes them away.

Thelewala is officially my new favorite spot for kathi rolls in NYC! 🌯🇮🇳

We tried the Thelewala Chicken Roll and Chapli Kebab Roll, and both were absolutely delicious! Freshly made, packed with flavor, and perfect for a quick, satisfying meal. Their chai was fabulous too—definitely worth ordering alongside your rolls. I was tempted to try the Chicken Phall Roll but will save that for my next visit!

The food is prepared fresh right in front of you, yet the service is quick. The space is small and casual, with the feel of a traditional thela (street-food cart) back home in India. It’s all about the food, with no fuss or frills.

only open 2 months and nearly 1,000 5-star reviews? a little suspicious... well, my partner and i decided to trust google maps, and man, did we regret it. $50+tip for 2 very disappointing bowls of ramen. the noodles and gyoza reminded us of the frozen variety — the noodles were excessively thick, hard to chew, and clumped together; the veggie gyoza were flavorless. raw arugula is an odd choice for topping — being bitter and having a dissatisfying texture — especially given that most ramen toppings (woodear mushrooms, bamboo shoots, bean sprouts, scallions, seaweed, spinach) are already vegan. their vegan meat/tofu mix was crumbling and disappearing into the broth. they add a performative bowl of smoke on top — it doesn't impart any flavor, but i did smell it on my fingernails and hair the rest of the night. the bowl didn't come together in either flavor or texture, and it's not worth $25. maybe it's okay if you have no other choice, but it falls far below standard compared to every other ramen shop in the city.

by the way — service was unconventional and limited — we ordered at a kiosk, sat at a table covered in cafeteria trays, and were served water from a self-service water dispenser in plastic cups. the ordering system seemed inefficient — the server could only take orders from one party at a time and made 3 parties of 2 stand outside in the rain, even though nearly all of the tables were empty — because you have to stand in a high-traffic area to order. it seemed confusing for everyone. it would probably be solved if they just seated everyone, then took orders at everyone's seats...

we left pretty quickly and actually walked to another ramen shop to satisfy our craving.

I was also concerned about the hygiene standards, as I saw the dog eating from plates on the table. This raised serious concerns for me about food hygiene and cleanliness.

Thankfully, we had not started eating before this incident occurred. What should have been a pleasant family outing turned into a very unpleasant and stressful experience.

Based on my experience, I would not recommend this restaurant to anyone. The owner's behavior was unacceptable, and the situation left us feeling unwelcome and uncomfortable. Customer service and hygiene should be basic priorities for any restaurant, and unfortunately, this experience fell far short of my expectations.

I would give zero stars if that were an option. I will never return and would strongly advise others to consider this experience before visiting.

Response to the Owner’s Comment:

When we decided to sit at your restaurant, none of us knew that stepping outside briefly to grab something from the car would apparently be such a SERIOUS issue. At the time, we were still settling into our table, and none of us had even placed an order yet. Some members of our group simply went to the car to get something for the children. It was a simple, innocent reason, not an attempt to disrespect you or your restaurant.

Are your customers expected to remain at their tables once they sit down, without even being allowed to step outside briefly before ordering? And if a few people step away to get something from their car while the group is still settling in, does that give you the right to dismiss the entire group and treat everyone so rudely?

Instead of making assumptions or escalating the situation, you could have simply asked us what was happening. A little understanding and basic courtesy would have made all the difference.

Your response, “Game over,” says a lot about how you chose to handle the situation. We were a group of adults with children, and we expected nothing more than a reasonable level of courtesy and respect. We had not ordered anything, caused no disturbance, or done anything to justify being treated in such an AGGRESSIVE and UNWELCOMING manner.

This experience was disappointing, and your response has only reinforced my concerns about your approach to customer service. A little patience and respectful communication would have gone a long way.

review_text:
Food is generally good, and quite spicy. We (party of 5) came here for dinner and had some hits but sadly, some misses too.
The service was atrocious.  It felt uneven at best. There was little coordination among the wait staff, dishes coming out haphazardly, appetizers came after some main dishes, and rice orders missing despite repeated requests. When a fish soup came, we had to go find a waitstaff to ask for bowls; the traditional Chinese bowls finally came but alas, with Western (metal) spoons.
The serving utensils too seemed afterthought: eating forks for soupy dishes, or in some cases, missing serving utensil altogether.
The underground venue, while spacious, was oddly arranged, as if it was hurriedly rearranged from something else. With glass mirror walls in enclosed space, it was not surprising that the noise level was quite unbearable at times.
We were seated at a round table, too large for our group of 5. Some chairs were clearly more suited for art studios (3-legged chairs make unstable dining chairs).

The food was good, but I would stick to takeout orders and skip the dine-in experience.

We were given two tables and soon one of the tables was given away to another group. Lastly, as if this wasn't enough, we were told that we had to leave within an hour because "reservations were valid for only 2 hours." The service and the manager were terrible in dealing with the situation. Every new interaction was a problem and we felt forced to leave the place. In a nutshell: terrible experience.

The pumpking keg blew my mind!!
Also the service was exceptional
Great pumpkin beer! Lots of fun
A superb Italian restaurant, delicious with authentic Italian flavors, I highly recommend it.

I visited Tre simply because its location was right next door to the hotel I was staying at. It’s a very small lowkey type of restaurant. I ordered the calamari. The ice cream itself also failed to impress us. Overall, we felt it was simply not good value for money. We had expected much more and cannot recommend a visit.
A wonderful experience!  My 6 year old friend enjoyed every little adventure that was offered and eating as much ice cream as he could!
We had an absolute blast with our teens and even as adults. Lots of places to take pics and we learned some things about ice cream. Try everything and have fun!!!!
My experience with my family was incredible, the place seems to never end, infinite ice cream and the staff of the place is very friendly, thank you ice cream museum

i had their chocolate chip cookies and they were very good. i always wanted to come because i saw it in the movie loser. yes i love my romantic comedies from the year 2000 :) but anyway very good place.

i also got their "rainbow" cookies. they were green and beige with the almond paste. so good! my parents loved them too. i also got the loaf of ciabatta bread. wow! i was blown away with how fresh it was. i brought it home. loved that there was so much flour on it too :). its my weakness. its so soft in the middle and crunchy on the outside. my parents went crazy over it. the only downside is that they don't slice it for you but its ok i still wanna buy it again!
Very good focaccia and pignoli cookies. Staff is always great

Enjoyed a really great pre-movie dinner here with a friend. Started with the beef tartare, which was great, then had the Caesar salad with grilled chicken, again fantastic, and ended with a delicious tangerine sorbet. It is pricey, but the food and atmosphere is fantastic. Highly recommend.
Ethan is the best server anywhere. Would recommend!

Ethan service was incredible. Loved the energy he brought to the table.

Great experience from start to finish. Ethan and Emmanuel took care of us. They were very prompt to seat and greet us:). I ordered the lunch combo (lentil soup and chicken salad tartine), it hit the spot! A great casual, but delicious vibe. Will be back!

I got the crispy chicken bowl with roasted sweet potatoes, and mac & cheese, with a green salad. Chicken and sweet potatoes were tasty, but both were warm, not really that hot. Also, the service yesterday was bad. The lady serving asked if I am ready, I said yes, so she came behind the corner as if she's doing me a favor. Then when I got to the protein section, when I asked what kind of fish this is, she answered, but stopped serving the order for a few minutes to fill all the containers that needed refill. Almost as retaliation for not being ready enough. The she proceeded to put the protein which is the last item.

I absolutely love the team at the Spring st location. I’m always greeted with smiles and good energy, not to mention that the food is always fresh and made to order. I believe the manger there name is Sue, she’s truly amazing and does a great job of creating a very healthy and fresh atmosphere.

DIG is one of the best places I’ve been for a fresh, satisfying meal and excellent service. The team is fast, friendly, and welcoming, and the generous portions offer outstanding value—especially in New York City.

At $14 for a bowl with four choices, or $17 for the salmon option, the pricing is hard to beat. Many restaurants charge $20–$25 for a single entrée, sometimes with additional charges for rice or sauces.

What truly stands out is the team’s commitment to their customers. They consistently go above and beyond to make sure you leave happy. Great food, fair prices, and exceptional service—I highly recommend it!
Great experience!!

very nice staff

One of the better dining halls at NYU. Most of the servers are pretty friendly and they have a nice variety of fresh food and different cuisines. Their knock-off CAVA bowls are pretty tasty. Chicken tenders are pretty fire. Coca-cola freestyle machine is super convenient. Would recommend.

Luis is the only serious burger maker. if you dont get him choose something else that day. Samba is also a very cool dude. Makes school not seem so hellish. Manhattan elegance without Manhattan prices. Five star food and service.  Maurizio is a delight.
Andrea was so kind to us!! She squeezed us in on a busy Wednesday night. The food was delish & her hospitality was even sweeter. Can’t wait to have the raggu pasta again!!

Had the worst restaurant experience ever in this place. Lousy service (we waited an hour for the food to arrive), food is mediocre at best, the space is super tight and uncomfortable and the price on some of the items we ordered were wrong! And here's the worst part: THEY CHARGED US 22% TIP INSTEAD OF THE 20% INDUSTRY STANDARD FOR A BIG GROUP! AND ON TOP OF THAT - THEY SLIPPED A $24 "HANDLING/CONVENIENCE FEE"! What kind of restaurant tries to slip a convenience fee on customers?! That is definitely ILLEGAL! The service, music, ambiance, and food here are absolutely amazing! From the moment we walked in, the staff was incredibly friendly and attentive, making us feel welcome right away.
Their cocktail game is top-tier, the drinks are perfectly balanced with a creative twist. We started with a dirty martini, a mezcal penicillin, and a glass of wine, all of which were excellent. For appetizers, we ordered the crispy tuna fries and the hamachi. Both were incredibly fresh, but what really stands out is how unique the sauces are. Everything is prepared to absolute perfection.
For our main course, we split the duck adobo and the fried rice, and it did not disappoint. During dinner, Chef Josh actually came over to our table to talk to us. He shared the inspiration behind the menu, explaining his incredible fusion of French and Filipino culinary styles, and mentioned that his mentor worked with Jean-Georges for a long time. You can truly taste that world-class pedigree in every single bite.
I highly recommend coming to this restaurant for an unforgettable meal. Plus, if you are looking to keep the night going, they transition into a club after 10 PM. We will definitely be back!
Great place I would definitely recommend coming here if your out in town
Great rewards program. Yummy vegan cookies and good coffee and matcha.
I got an iced vanilla latte with extra ice and sugar free vanilla with almond milk and a cookie butter cookie. The cookie is tasty. However the latte is way too sweet and milky.

HOW have I slept on this place for so long?? service was excellent and everything I tried was beyond delicious. Best meal I have had in ages. Already plotting how I can make my next visit with a big group so I can try more dishes.

It is not a Romanian restaurant.

Took my dad out for dinner here for his birthday…we are Romanian and this restaurant is “Romanian-ish” which we appreciated!! Very tasty food that did not disappoint. Loved the vibe and the fact that it’s tapas style: shareable little plates. Our favorite was the stuffed pepper: both sweet and smoky and delicious. The fasole batuta which is a bean dip tasted very authentic. My dad looooved the burrata. The mici (little Romanian sausages) did not taste very much like the mici we are used to but they were fine, even  better paired with the pickled spicy grapes. Mamaliga was delicious. Service was great. They knew we were celebrating a birthday and brought over a little plate with gummy bears and a lit candle, super thoughtful gesture and very appreciated. Loved the whole dining experience here and would absolutely return and recommend.
Really well executed, unique brunch items, lovely one man show.

It’s difficult to put into a short review how wonderful this restaurant is and how delicious their food is. You perfectly encapsulate every yummy flavor that is Romanian food. It’s the most intimate cozy lovely little gem. I grew up on my mom and bunică‘s Romanian home-cooked meals, and all the dishes at Oti taste just like those sentimental dishes from my childhood, but with a unique and thoughtful twist.
Please go eat there. I’m always proud to be Romanian, and this little restaurant quietly nestled in the Lower East Side makes me even more proud and reminds me of home.
Best service with George and Fernando! Football Sunday was a great time! Can’t recommend this place for the food and service!

We made a reservation for Sunday brunch at noon - not a night out at a bar. Nowhere we checked online or during the reservation process did we see any notice that this restaurant was strictly 21+. Yet after our group had already been seated, we were told to leave because one person was under 21. We were there for a meal, and no one in our party was drinking.

The lack of communication was frustrating enough, but the way we were treated was unacceptable. The security guard laughed and told us he was being "nice” by kicking that person out because he was feeling good that day. There was nothing nice about humiliating a group of customers over a policy that had never been communicated to them.

If your restaurant has a strict age restriction - even for Sunday brunch - make it clear on your website, on your reservation page, and before seating your guests. Customers should not have to discover your entry policy through a condescending interaction after they’ve already arrived and sat down. A wasted reservation and an incredibly disappointing experience.

The pizza here is just phenomenal. I think this may be my new absolute favorite NY pizzeria. We had their Roman style rectangular pizza with several different toppings. This is a very crunchy style of pizza which is about half inch thick but very light and crispy. The crust was absolutely amazing, thanks to a very high hydration dough (I asked the server). It was airy, light, crunchy, salty. This may have been the best crust I’ve ever had. And the toppings were all excellent, from nduja and zucchini to the plain Margherita. I cannot recommend this place enough!

As a Japanese person, Yopparai made me feel a little homesick — in the best possible way.

From the moment I walked in, the atmosphere reminded me of an izakaya back home in Japan. Warm, intimate, and so authentically Japanese that for a little while, I almost forgot I was in New York.

The food made that feeling even stronger. The tempura was perfectly light and crispy, and the oden was absolutely delicious, with the broth and flavor soaked into every bite. Paired with Japanese sake, it was just perfect.

There was something very special about being able to enjoy the kind of delicious food I would eat in Japan, right here in New York. As someone from Japan, it genuinely made me happy and brought back memories of home.

Yopparai isn’t just a place to eat Japanese food — it’s a place where you can experience the warmth and comfort of a real Japanese izakaya.

Great food, great sake, and a wonderful atmosphere. If you’re looking for an authentic izakaya experience in New York, I highly recommend Yopparai.

After scouring the New York dining scene to pick the right restaurant for a weekend trip in NYC, Corima caught my eye. Great location, stylish dining room, and an original menu in a city with a myriad of mediocre, overpriced Mexican.

At the suggestion of our server, we bought into the tasting menu with drink pairing (mostly because he said it was the only part of the menu that included a taco). As a product of the US-Mexico border, the concept of high-end north Mexican food seemed intriguing, but ultimately fell flat. Several poorly-paced courses and $600 later, we left hungry and disappointed. This felt like everything wrong with NYC’s overhyped dining scene, and the fact that a tortilla was the best and most original thing on the menu was insulting. I do not understand the hype, and the accolades continue to confuse me.

**Taco pictured for reference.

Got the tasting menu with the alcohol tasting pairing menu too.

The meal was amazing. Many small courses and small shots of tequilas to pair with it.

So many interesting exotic and unusual but delicious flavors.

Will come back and take some friends/family too.

The food at Corima is honestly wonderful: creative, surprising and, most importantly, really delicious. There were several dishes I absolutely loved, which is why I was a little sad that the overall experience didn’t quite feel like five stars to me. The food itself is the clear highlight, and I would genuinely love to return, especially to try the à la carte menu.

The tasting menu included some excellent and memorable dishes. However, I didn’t realise when booking through Resy that the tasting menu was the only option attached to our reservation. We weren’t shown a food menu or asked whether we preferred the tasting menu or à la carte. Later, I saw the couple next to us enjoying beautiful full-sized dishes and realised that à la carte was also available. Maybe I missed something while booking, but I really wish I had known, as their dinner looked like my dream meal. Personally, I would much rather have three amazing dishes and more than one bite of each than thirteen tiny courses.

Unfortunately, the service and communication sometimes felt less polished than I had expected. When we arrived, there was nobody at the entrance, so we — along with another couple — walked into the restaurant before eventually coming back to find someone.

I had also mentioned some food intolerances in my reservation and was told that the restaurant had tried several times to contact me by phone and email. I may have missed calls while travelling, but I never received an email. In the end, I explained that they were intolerances rather than allergies and that I could be flexible, so it wasn’t really an issue, it was just the communication side that felt a little odd.

There were also a few moments during the meal when clearer communication would have helped. We ordered the tortilla with caviar after seeing it at the table next to us. It arrived without caviar and without explanation. We asked again and ordered another one with caviar, but that one also arrived without it. Only when we asked a second time were we told that they had run out. Of course, restaurants run out of things, and that is absolutely no problem; I would simply have appreciated being told before the dish arrived twice.

Something similar happened when we asked to add one of the à la carte dishes we had seen at the neighbouring table. We made clear that we didn’t want to change the tasting menu, but simply wanted to add and pay for another dish. We were told that someone would check, but nobody came back to us. Once dessert arrived, we understood that it wasn’t happening.

None of these things individually is a major issue, and everyone on the team was genuinely lovely and kind. I think I simply expected the experience to feel a little more effortless and attentive at a Michelin-starred restaurant. The food absolutely deserves the praise, and I would happily come back to Corima, particularly to try the à la carte menu. I just wish the service and communication had been a little more refined and had made us feel slightly more looked after, because with food this good, that would have made the evening exceptional.

I liked the room, which is annoying in retrospect. It was small, a little cramped, and full of the kind of references I grew up around in family restaurants. For a minute it felt quaint, familiar, like somebody’s actual kitchen. The meal did not survive that impression.

We had come for the fusion, that New York meeting of Hispanic and Chinese food, which is hardly a wild idea in this city. You would think someone in the building could talk about it. The waitress could not. Questions got hesitant, flummoxed half-answers, with no opinion and no sense of what was worth ordering. She set the plates down and left. Water was not refilled. A premade iced tea and a straw took about ten minutes. We were in the back booth by the bathroom, along one narrow walkway, so there was nowhere for her to pretend she was not passing us. She did, ten or twelve times, without a word, clearly clocking whether we were done. In a room that small, a stare is not subtle. The attention arrived for the exit and never for the meal. It felt scrutinized, and a little discriminatory.

The portions were generous for the price, and that is the only credit I will give. The food was greasy, overcooked, and mushy, oversalted and still underseasoned, with a gamey edge that belonged to neither tradition. The broccoli beside the sesame chicken was the best thing on the table, which is a miserable thing to have to admit. Everything else tasted like a five-minute search for the dish it was supposed to be. A bastardization. The drinks were the same failure in a glass: too tart and sour, or so sweet the fruit had disappeared.

I can speak for the Chinese side. The people with me can speak for the Hispanic side. None of us took this as gospel, and none of us were impressed. This city already has rooms that love both cuisines, and rooms that fuse them without embarrassing either one. This was the neighborhood worn as a costume. An overrated cash grab, with none of the love and none of the craft. I would not go back.

My personal favorite was the tuna tacos — absolutely delicious.The least impressive for me was the cactus shaped cookie, although it was certainly very creative and beautifully presented.

Overall, the experience was exceptional.The atmosphere was unique and special, and the staff were incredibly friendly, attentive, and welcoming. A wonderful place for a memorable evening.
Good old fashioned diner.
Our home base when visiting NYC. We've tried different menu items every day and it's all been incredible. Everyone is super friendly too, especially Roberto
The food was delicious and the service was wonderful. We went with our child, and everyone was very kind and welcoming. We had a lovely experience!

We waited outside on the line  for 45 minutes just to write our name then waited an additional One hour to be called and then was told there’s only seating outside available. We sat in a container outside. The sun was in my face the whole time while I was eating and the food was super overrated. I mean, the food is not worth the Wait but the prices are ok THE PANCAKES were NOT what I expected the syrup what’s the best thing about it and I’m just being 100% honest
Long wait (1.5 hours) but the food was really effing solid. Especially the pancakes. So good so good. Korean chicken was great as well as was the club sandwich

The pancakes were worth the 1 and a half hours wait our party if 7 were taken care of as soon as we were seated. Ordering was quick and the food came out in sooner than we thought. We all order the pancakes and am the other breakfast plates. The star of the show were the pancakes they were melt in your mouth and not too sweet.
First time here today food did not disappoint! Was definitely worth the wait very good!
Food and service were amazing, portions on the pancakes were very generous

Went as a family of 5, was yummy food outside of the avocado toast. Nice seating outside, especially in the sun. Rude staff when it comes to tipping, felt personal till I read other reviews and they all talk about the same guy so I’m not surprised.

Unfortunately, it was really not good. Far too expensive for poor to mediocre food. The waiter also wanted to give himself a larger tip and only reluctantly gave us the change after we asked several times.

I’ve seen it’s a pattern in the reviews that flies make their way into the dishes. I have now seen this firsthand. Two flies in my avocado toast. The fly wouldn’t even eat the food and appeared unalive upon impact with the thing they call an egg that was thrust upon my plate. I am livid.

I had heard really great things about this place and I was excited to try it on my last trip to New York, unfortunately, my experience was not great.

The food was actually really good—really decent portions, and some great vegan/vegetarian options. My main issue with my experience was the service and the atmosphere.

I was dining solo for brunch on a Sunday (a few weeks ago now) and noted that the patio and indoor seating were not full. I asked to sit on the patio if they had the space and the hostess was very short with me. She brought me out to this one patio table that was completely cut off from the rest of the tables, it had no umbrella and instead of regular chairs it had these little stools. It was at least 10 feet away from the other tables, on the opposite side of the door they use when delivering food to the patio. I want to note that the other patio seats were not full, and there were a number of additional options for me to be seated. I wouldn’t have minded the weird placement of the table if I were not dining solo—it seemed like a strange choice to seat the solo diner in the far corner of the patio (it honestly didn’t even feel like it was part of the patio, I might as well have been eating on the sidewalk).

The waitress was only polite when it came time to pay the bill. She seemed annoyed when I ordered my coffee first and needed another minute with the food menu.

About halfway through my meal, I wanted to ask to move inside since the fully exposed dunce corner seat was in direct sunlight and giving me a sunburn. I didn’t get the chance, since the waitress didn’t return for another 20 minutes or so. I just asked for the bill.

Since I’ve been a waitress, I tipped her well (i’m not a monster who doesn’t tip, even if the service sucks), which was the point of the interaction I got a brief smile, followed by her quickly leaving.

Honestly, I have a lot of patience for bad service usually, and I found the service in New York to be extremely courteous and lovely aside from this one experience. I just haven’t been able to get this meal out of my head since I ate there some weeks ago now.

I echo what some other commenters have said regarding the service. I think some training is needed, and perhaps adding another table to that very sad seating area where I was placed.
They were sold out of several flavors, but it’s always nice to have access to vegan ice cream (and cookies!) anywhere in the city. The ice cream is so creamy (not icy) for a vegan ice cream, too!
One of the best ice creams I've ever had! The honeycomb and Earl Grey flavors are amazing!
Nice ice cream
Hahaha I love the ice cream here and how Alice treat us 🥺❤️ everything was very clean and she was super kind
Some of the best ice cream in New York with unique flavors  and vegan options
AMZING THANK YOU IBRAHIM
Zara pizza is the best pizza in the city. Ibrahim the best!
American pizza at a reasonable price.
Delicious
Ramos makes the best pizza in town.
They have a bathroom and love when people go in and use it without purchasing anything

I get to finally get in touch with the writing author in me. A creative artist that can dance silently via the ink of a pen. I love to take their writing classes, buy a nice trinket, glitter pens, a cappuccino, a good book & get cozy on the couch. Scholar mode activated. Grateful. 🌟🌸🌟📝📚☕️
Super friendly staff, one of the most delicious Matchas I‘ve ever had, perfect place to read or study

Came with one of my friends. There was no wait time. Definitely get the spring rolls because they are bomb. The lemon soda is good too, and I get my classic number one, which is nothing special, but it fills you up.
Vegan dishes are great. Taste and texture was pretty on point even for a ethnic Vietnamese person if that means anything. Would go again and recommend to others

I arrived at 5 PM and had dinner with friends. The restaurant wasn't very crowded, even though I had a reservation. The menu had many dishes. I ordered Hue-style beef noodle soup, grilled pork noodle soup, crab noodle soup, chicken pho, and grilled chicken rice. The grilled pork noodle soup and Hue-style beef noodle soup were very flavorful. The chicken pho wasn't outstanding. The service was quick but not very friendly. The space was a bit simple. I think if I wanted to eat pho, I would go to a better restaurant.
Number 1 and thai iced tea for the win! One of the best in the city
The map-guided reservation was made by a different company.

I absolutely love this place! It truly feels like being in Japan. I’ve visited for both lunch and dinner, and every experience has been wonderful.

The drinks are exceptional — especially the buckwheat drink. I had it over a year ago and still remember how good it was!

The food is beautifully executed, and you can tell a lot of care goes into every detail. Even the side dishes feel thoughtful and well-crafted.

My favorite is the mochi soup. It was absolutely phenomenal and tasted just like the one I had in Japan. 🥰💗

This is one of those places that keeps you coming back. Highly recommend!

Came here for the Uni Don, but the food was mediocre and the staff is straight-up trash.

There was zero service, so I left a minimal tip. The waitress literally hovered over me like a hawk, staring dead at my hands while I signed. When she saw the amount, she actually had the audacity to confront me, then immediately ganged up with the chef to laugh and mock me right to my face.

To bully and humiliate a paying customer for your own garbage performance is incredibly toxic and unprofessional. These people are pathetic and have zero basic respect. Avoid this place like the plague.
Amazing!

One of the best omakases in NYC, and one of only a few that serve a variety of authentic Japanese dishes (as most other omakases in NYC are very sushi heavy). Every single item on the menu is of excellent quality with artful presentation and attentive service
Chicken was very CHEWY and not CRISPY I woke up today having server diarrhea and throwing up . Usually this place is good but cleary the food was rushed .
The best chicken spot in soho nyc
da best
Love it here

Took a friend who’s Celiac and eats gluten free here and she said it was amazing, so if you are as well then I would definitely recommend. However, we all agreed that the price for the portions we received were INSANE. Too small and wildly overpriced.

My soup was delicious, however, the portion was grossly misleading and incredibly shallow. The tip of the spoon barely went in it, like there’s no way it was even a centimeter deep, I’m not even exaggerating. I actually found it hard to eat it because I couldn’t scrape the spoon it the bowl enough lol.

We went here for the promise of gluten free, and it delivered on that at least.

What it didn’t deliver was appropriate pricing for any item on the menu.

The $20 bruschette were on four slices of bread the size of potato chips. The $23 soup was only a centimeter deep. The $38 rigatoni ai funghi left me hungrier than when I arrived
The best G-F food I've had anywhere! Great service, ambiance. The pasta dough is to die for.

I cannot say enough good things about this restaurant. Having a 100% gluten free Italian restaurant in NYC was like a dream come true. And, they even had a nice, soft, warm bread for the table. The lasagna was fantastic!
Great night of comedy!  If you're looking to laugh and let loose, then go here!
Great place to have a good time
I really like visiting this place! Amazing coffee and bakery!
Great service, nice pastries and kind staff!
A most fun informative croissant class. Chef Nicholas was great, helpful, patient and class was fun.
Good wfh spot but limited working outlets. The coffee was good, theres wifi and a bathroom. Would go back
unfriendly barista, drip coffee is fine, nothing special
The pumpkin spice latte was to die for… possibly the best latte I’ve ever had. There’s also a lot of space inside to sit and work! Obsessed 🩷
The worst service I've ever seen.

Wow! The best Italian food outside of Italy! Their house red sauce is the best sauce I've ever had, and on top of the lasagne, it really felt like I was back in Italy.
The desserts are also amazing! We had the lemon tiramisu, which was so fresh and flavourful, and the house chocolate cake (I can't remember the official name), but it was the best chocolate dessert I've had in a long time!
I can't explain enough how authentic and fresh the food tastes. It is pretty expensive, but you can really tell how much time and effort goes in to perfecting each dish and that's fairly reflected in the price.

Honestly, I feel terrible to write this, I've never done it before, but I literally had the worst experience possible in this place.
The prices are skyrocketing high, yet the portions are small and not satisfactory at all.
I ordered one dish that got me disgusted just by looking at it, the tables were sticky, the dishes were dirty.
I don't remember the last time I had such a horrible horrible experience, I don't know how people even write that they're food is good, the whole experience was just one big disappointment.

I am puzzled by the reviews that I read. Our experience was not very good. We were the only people in the restaurant. The service was odd at best.  We ordered one eggplant parm entree and two soft drinks. The food was warmed from the freezer. It came with nothing other than a square of eggplant parm. The bill was $58 for that pathetic plate of food. It did not taste terrible but it was not priced appropriately. Even giving us a bill was a challenge for the establishment. It was such a sad experience it was almost funny. I would not recommend eating anything there.
So sad ATLA is gone. Real NoHo gem!
Just a great spit..everydish was awesome.  Flavor bombs great technique and layering. Can't wait to go back before they close
Great sandwiches and bread but stop ripping people off with $5.50 bottles of Arkansas spring water!! Jeez!! It’s $2.50 at wholefoods who are already expensive
Dry dry bread
Really enjoyed my visit! The coffee was excellent, and the staff was very friendly. Definitely recommend this place!

Do not order ever delivery from Cafe D’Avignon! They never update their inventory or menus on all the delivery apps and either only deliver one out of five things you ordered (so you’re paying $12 in fees and tip for one croissant, plus the cost of the croissant!!) or they cancel your order 40 minutes or more after you placed it. TERRIBLE delivery. They never call you, they show zero courtesy to customers. They should not be on any delivery apps- they’re not equipped at all to be on delivery apps. So badly managed. They don’t update inventory or call you if they’re out of what you ordered.
A lovely place to grab some baked goods and a coffee, thank you! The staff was very nice.
The service at this restaurant is quite average and rigid, which doesn't seem worth it for the price. Plus, the food isn't as good as expected.

Amazing sushi, worth the expensive price. Each item was delicious and perfectly presented. The chefs are friendly and extremely attentive. My favorite pieces were the ankimo, sawara, chutoro, nodoguro, anago, and basque cheesecake. Would definitely come back.

Such a great experience. The fish was incredible, every course was on point, and the service made the whole night even better. Everyone was warm, knowledgeable, and made you feel really comfortable at the counter.

Definitely not an everyday dinner, but if you love sushi and want to treat yourself, Yoshino is absolutely worth experiencing. One of the best omakase meals I’ve had in NYC and I’d definitely go back.

Incredible omakase experience, truly on another level. Every course was so finely prepared with each being more delicious than the last. Attentive service, intimate atmosphere, and a friendly chef who is clearly a master of his craft. We hope to return soon!

We had a reservation booked and paid for for tonight at 9pm. literally 10 minutes before the reservation, as we’ve already almost arrived at the restaurant, hungry and looking forward to this reservation, we receive a call saying they forgot to close reservations on Resy and there’s no availability for us anymore (which seems odd/suspicious). There’s was no offer to alleviate our inconvenience, wasted time and derailment of our night here. Now it’s 9pm and we’re scrambling trying to find a restaurant reservation for now. This is horrible operations for a Michelin star restaurant and we are massively disappointed. The reservation name was under Carson.

Incredibly exceptional yakitori omakase. Michellin-starred for good reason. The chef cooked every piece of yakitori to perfection and there's always something beautiful about cooking over an open fire. 12-Course Omakase for $189 PP. Worth every penny. There is so much love that goes into cooking each and every yakitori. I thoroughly enjoyed how different and special every course felt and tasted. And oh my goodness, that bowl of soup and noodles at the end is amazingly delicious. We were extremely full and I was quite sad to let my husband eat the rest of my noodles.

Service was absolutely perfect -- professional, attentive, and warm. I also enjoyed the space. Very peaceful and calming. There's one long wooden counter where you get to watch the chefs in action.

Loved this dining experience and can't wait to go back.

First time dined at Torien on my husband’s birthday and we had a blast. Both service and foods were phenomenal. My chef Hideo is excellent and definitely will be back again soon:)

The staff is goated, and the food is great. Get the charred chicken mac and cheese and sweet potatoes.

I found true authentic cooking here. This place surpassed all expectations. Staff is accommodating, real, and sincere. We've built trusting relationships with people here. This restaurant deserves discovery!

The cooks make the food worth eating and the servers make you feel valued. The employees were efficient yet warm in their service. Satisfying experience. This restaurant serves fresh food without the premium markup. This place represents the height of quality.

The tuna over crispy tapioca, cassava fries with açaí ketchup and the moqueca with dry aged fish were my favorites. And also the flan with sesame, yum.

Can’t wait to go back!
This was some of the most delicious Brazilian food I’ve ever had.

What a great restaurant, Alana I hope I spelled it correctly was so great! She gave such good recommendations for the food. Everything was genuinely so delicious from drinks to desserts. Every waiter was so attentive and so friendly. I hope they get on the Michelin list or at least recommendations they fully deserve it.

This spot is unassuming but upstairs is a speakeasy with a gorgeous interior and intimate vibes. We tried the Crystal Peach Oolong and Osmanthus Yuzu Fizz, and both were SO good. The flavors were incredible, but don’t let how smooth they taste fool you because they’re STRONG!  Each drink also came with a little card explaining its ingredients and flavor profile, which was such a nice touch.

We ordered a variety of bites, and everything was delicious! The Miso Sake Kama had perfectly crispy skin, while the Roku Ebi was incredibly crispy and satisfying. The Chicken Truffle Ramen had a lighter, clean-tasting broth with bouncy noodles that made every bite so enjoyable. The rolls were delicious too, and we went with the staff’s recommendations. The service was incredible from start to finish!

Definitely a great spot for creative cocktails, Japanese bites, and a gorgeous atmosphere for your next night out in NYC!

I absolutely love Dudley’s! I come here at least once a month, and it has easily become one of my favorite restaurants over the past 2–3 years. The food, service, and atmosphere are consistently great, and I’ve introduced so many friends to this place.

That being said, I think being such a regular customer allows me to offer some honest feedback.

On one occasion, I found a hair wrapped around my pancake after I had already covered it in syrup and was about to take my first bite. Of course, it was disappointing, but the staff handled it well, replaced my meal, and took it off the bill. Clearly, it didn’t stop me from coming back!

My biggest frustration is the inability to make reservations in the morning. I completely understand how busy brunch can get, especially on weekends and holidays, but I wish there were some flexibility. I tried making a reservation for Mother’s Day because I wanted to bring my mom, but unfortunately, that wasn’t an option.

I also wanted to mention the menu changes following the renovations. The restaurant itself looks beautiful, and I appreciate the updates, but I genuinely miss the original steak frites. It used to be one of my favorite dishes on the menu! While I appreciate the addition of the smothered steak, the changes to the steak frites have been disappointing, and I’ve found myself coming in for dinner much less frequently because of it.

Despite these few critiques, I really do love Dudley’s. It’s a place I consistently return to, recommend to others, and genuinely enjoy supporting. I was just here yesterday and I’m already coming back today!

I hope this feedback is received in the spirit it’s intended. I’m sharing it because I’ve been a loyal customer for years and would love to see a few of the things that originally made this place so special return. Dudley’s is still one of my favorites, and I look forward to many more visits!

Understandably, the entire bar was upset and asking questions after the announcement. The woman with brown hair, who I assume was the manager, was incredibly unapologetic. She grabbed the remote, turned off the Knicks game, and told everyone to leave. The way the situation was handled felt unnecessarily rude and dismissive.

This would have been a completely different situation if the bar had simply disclosed upfront that there was a private event and that patrons would need to leave before or during the game. To kick people out in the middle of the Knicks finals and force them to scramble to find another bar, without any prior warning, is awful customer service.

What makes this even more frustrating is that Bonnie Vee had posted on Instagram that the Knicks game would be on at the bar. Had we known we wouldn't actually be able to watch it there, we never would have come in the first place.

Misleading Menu Description and Server

I placed a pickup order through Grubhub for a beef and lamb lava, which was advertised as" Slide of lamb gyro in side fresh homemade lava Jerusalem salad finish with tahini and homemade hot sauce sauce + fries". The online description and picture clearly showed these items included in the meal.

I walked over 10 minutes to pick up my order and then walked back home, only to discover that the sauces and fries were missing. I had to walk all the way back to the restaurant and show the server the menu description on Grubhub. Instead of acknowledging the discrepancy, the server insisted that some fries were inside the gyro and that I had to pay extra for fries on the side as the picture.

I showed him the actual description, which explicitly stated that the meal included fries. I returned home again and, guess what? There wasn't a single fry inside the gyro.

I don't mind paying extra for fries, but the menu needs to be clear and accurate. If fries are not included, they should not be listed in the description or shown in the picture as part of the meal. Customers should not have to waste their time making two trips because of misleading advertising.

This one honestly hurt my heart…

Y’all… this review hurts my heart to write because I am a Sweet Chick fan.

Not a “I tried it once” fan. A real fan.

I’ve been going to Sweet Chick since there was only one location in Brooklyn. I was literally traveling from Jersey to Brooklyn just for the food, the drinks, and the experience, and I never minded doing it because it was always worth it.

So when they opened the Ludlow Street location, I was excited because now I didn’t have to make the trip to Brooklyn every time I wanted my chicken and waffles.

Back then, Sweet Chick was an experience.

They had the big specials board with rotating waffles, desserts, and seasonal items. Their chicken and waffles never missed. I honestly can’t remember ever leaving disappointed.

So this review is really hard for me.

Back on June 26th, after work, my mom and I decided to grab dinner. I work in the LES, and she suggested Sweet Chick. I did tell her my brother Robert had gone recently and said it had changed a lot, but we figured we’d see for ourselves.

We got there around 9-ish.

The first thing we noticed…

It was HOT.

Not warm.

Hot.

Like, “why does it feel like a sauna in here?” hot.

We’ve had enough hot weather this summer, so walking into a restaurant with little to no air conditioning was honestly uncomfortable. We actually debated leaving before we even ordered, but decided to stick it out.

Unfortunately… it never got better.

The service also wasn’t what I remembered.

I’m really big on customer service, and Sweet Chick has always had amazing service whenever I’ve gone. This time it just felt different. The attentiveness wasn’t there, and the overall vibe just felt… off.

Even the menu has changed.

My mom used to love their kale salad, but now it’s made differently with things like dates, and she wasn’t interested in it anymore.

For drinks, my mom ordered an espresso martini, and unfortunately she really didn’t enjoy it. It was pretty bitter, and we couldn’t quite figure out what was off about it. If I’m ordering an espresso martini, I have certain expectations, and this one just didn’t hit for her.

I ordered the Queen of New York, and I actually really enjoyed my drink. No complaints there.

Now… the food.

I ordered the Maple Chipotle Chicken & Sweet Potato Waffle.

And this is where my heart really broke.

Years ago, when they first introduced the sweet potato waffle as a special, I remember it actually tasting like sweet potato.

This one…

Honestly just tasted like a regular waffle.

I kept looking for that sweet potato flavor, and it just wasn’t there.

The chicken itself was crispy and cooked well, but the maple chipotle sauce wasn’t evenly coated. Some bites were really good, while other pieces were dry because they barely had any sauce on them.

Another thing longtime Sweet Chick fans might notice is the butter service.

I remember getting three or four different flavored butters, each in their own little container.

This time we got two flavors together in one cup.

It’s a small thing, but it was one of those details that always made Sweet Chick feel special.

My mom ordered the Carolina BBQ Chicken with the Grilled Corn Waffle.

I’ll be fair—her waffle absolutely tasted like a corn waffle. I tried it, and it was really good.

She enjoyed her meal more than I did, although she also had a few pieces of chicken that weren’t evenly coated with sauce and were a little dry.

Overall, she thought it was okay.

And I think that’s really the word for this visit.

Okay.

Not terrible.

But not the Sweet Chick we remembered.

Maybe that’s why this visit hit me so hard.

When you’ve loved a place for years, you naturally compare it to what you know it can be.

I genuinely hope this was just an off night because I have so many great memories here, and I’d honestly love to come back one day and have the Sweet Chick experience that made me fall in love with it in the first place.

Because this restaurant has meant a lot to me over the years, and I’m rooting for it.

I really am.

I thought I didn’t like matcha until I tried this place! The baristas pointed me in the right direction. I’ll definitely be coming back! Thanks everyone
cute spot! matcha was so yum & the baristas were super nice— great service :))

Doorman has an ego issue. He will stare you down and refuse to open the door; not sure if it’s because I’m East Asian or the way I was dressed, but he made it clear I was “undeserving” of him opening the door. We spend a significant amount of money at Kith; I shouldn’t need to look a certain way to be treated like a normal customer. It’s left a sour taste in my mouth and I find it hard to continue splurging so much on a brand where the first person you interact with acts like he’s better than you. Management seriously needs to evaluate who they put as the face of the store.

Kith Manhattan is hands down one of the best retail experiences in NYC. The vibe feels more like a modern gallery than a standard boutique, elevated by an incredible mix of sleek marble, warm wood, brass accents, and industrial metal fixtures.
The curation is unmatched—from the iconic sneaker wall and Kith's in-house collections to high-end designer apparel and standout accessories. An absolute must-visit in Soho.
Great place for breakfast. I had congee, chow mein and HK milk tee for a total of $10
Hong Kong Flavor

Authentic , great breakfast food, got the pork chop.
The coffee pretty good too.
Definitely will be back to try more

Cheaper than HK for some things. Come early cause things are sold out in the afternoon. I like the beef chow fun which can be a little more charred. The soup with grilled chicken. The HK milk tea is the best for the area, the hot one. The cold one is a hit or miss depending on who is making it.

They don't have the $30 wine Wednesday deal anymore heads up, it's still on their website site but they don't honor it. Went for HH and they were out of the cocktail we ordered? It's 6oclock? Much better bars elsewhere PASS.

Great cocktails, super interesting in both flavors and names. But the real star of the show is the Thursday-Saturday server Addie who is amazing and deserves the world & has gone out of her way to make sure my friends and I (and everyone else) have a great time every time we stop in
Max is my favorite employee. What a wonderful establishment. The whole team is great!
Bartender Esteban is an awesome guy. Makes great drinks
Had a fantastic experience Tonight. Great vibes and Esteban is probably the greatest bartender in New York. He absolutely deserves a raise.

Blue Road Burger was a great experience. I went in after randomly picking where to eat and it was such a nice experience. The food was 10/10. Fries were super good, burger? SUPER GOOD. Fast service. I won’t give it 5 stars for atmosphere because there’s a lot of people smoking outside, and even if you’re sitting in the back the smell is really strong, but there’s nothing they can really do about it.

One of the best chicken Caesar wraps in the city. They have great burgers and fries too. Everything is made fresh, fast, and with great service. Beer is $5, what else could you ask for. Highly recommend as a dinner or late night spot!

I 100% recommend this place, I got the chicken sandwich and the meat was perfectly cooked and juicy, the prices are very affordable and the lady working that day gives an excellent customer service. 🌟 🌟 🌟 🌟 🌟
Bloody good burger! Solid flavors and I’m a burger snob.
Amazing spot for drinks!!
This place is so amazing. Pleade order cocktails from the manu and you wouldn't get disappointed.
Feels like ur going to another country, friendly staff
Great drinks and music! The place gets crowded, so come early if you want a seat. Definitely recommend trying their signature cocktails.
Best dumplings we had in Chinatown. Well worth the hype. Very reasonable prices, highly recommend to anyone in the area

Beef pancake was fantastic flavor: 9/10
Pork soup dumplings, okay, extremely underwhelming: 6/10
Spicy chicken huimei: 6/10
Beef brisket hui mein: 6/10
Wouldn’t go back unless just for beef pancake, better options in Chinatown
Also only space for 20 people total
Delicious and authentic Chinese food!

The must have dish is their spicy chicken tray. It's a lot of food so I recommend at least two people eating this and ordering lots of handpulled noodles on the side. Always ask for the noodles on the side so it doesn't get soggy. I also love their dumplings and oxtail soup with lamb broth.
The best Italian food I have had since I can’t remember. Everything we had was sublime.

Came to il Buco with high expectations and they were exceeded. A friend whose opinion on these things I trust has been coming here for years and I had heard the name, so I was excited to finally check it out.

We started with a glass of red that he chose for us and then ordered the little ham and cheese sandwiches, the pulpo and kale Caesar to start along with the house bread. For the main we had the special pasta with bone marrow and mushroom and the 40 ounce ribeye which was honestly too much food but all delicious.

Our server Christian was super helpful and made sure our glasses of wine were never empty. My one bit of feedback would be about noise level but other than that, a great meal.
The best slices I had while in NYC. Fast and friendly service. Clean restroom.
David is the best and the pizza is the best
Amazing crew and absolutely love the pizza. David the king is the best in the city

Needing to find a storage quickly and not too far from my place, I  wrote an email on a Sunday, asking for informations and availability in the lower east side storage.
Samuel (the owner!) responded me in only a few minutes, we exchanged very easily and he helped me to get in a few weeks the only space which will be freed very soon.
I was so happy and relieved !
Can’t share anything about the facility for the moment but in terms of customer service I recommend very likely, as the human side is very important to me and changes everything!
Sam, the owner, is so kind. He gave me a tour of the facility, because I wanted to see it before signing. It was clean and easy to access. I’m looking forward to moving my stuff in soon.
Clean, convenient and right sized. Owner (Sam) is open and honest. No hidden fees or gimmicks.

Really good experience with S2 Storage on Stanton. The lockers are new and clean, and getting set up was super easy. Sam was quick to reply and helpful the whole way. Definitely recommend if you need some extra space in the area.
such a great experience! Sam is super helpful and 24/7 assistance. the storage is great and central location. very easy to use and super great price. will use for my storage needs in NYC!!
Super friendly staff anf yummy macaroni

The macarons are great - freshly made and the almond flavour shines through beautifully

the ice cream is a must! The macaron ice cream was so good - delicious almond ice cream with bits of macaron...we were in awe!

Sorbets are good as well and beautifully balanced.

Service is really friendly as well.

A must stop when in Soho.

What a beautiful adorable store that had a great feel.
Amazing selection of Macarons and beautiful Chocolates in gift sets and wonderful set for those special occasions like valentines day and that perfect selection of dark and Milk chocolate all made fresh and locally.
Very nice and the nutella hot chocolate was very good. Apart from that the espresso is the cheapest we have found in downtown NY
Hello it's Milton. I came here a few years ago and just had a dream about when I came. It was an OK dream. Not too bad, not too good. Just a little bit mediocre. Goodbye it's Milton.
Delicious food, but the service was terrible! 🙈🙈🙈

The other appetizer we tried was just okay as well, with the meat being pretty tough. Overall, there were some good elements, but the meal was underwhelming for the price.

Very quick service when you’re looking for a fast bite, but never too busy that you can’t have a long talk with a friend over a nice bowl of soup. Noodles have great chewy texture. Rice plates are big portions and very filling.
It's getting worse and worse. The boiled fish was almost gone, like it'd been stolen. It was all bean sprouts, and they were half-cooked, not even cooked properly. It tasted raw.

Food is just ok.
Place looks like needing a great make over for a long time.
Pleasant and open late.
Had an incredibly great time so happy I was able to go. Everything was perfect.

I came from out of town for a week and this ended up being my go to bar for the week the people made me feel like home and I greatly appreciated everything they did for me while I was there it was truly a great time and can’t thank the staff there enough
They didn’t honor their happy hour deal during the World Cup :/
Great place to catch a drink after work! 🍻

I love the vibe so I SO badly wanted to love this place but just absolutely AWFUL service. The bartender during the world cup game on Saturday, 7/18, was the most miserable person on the planet and just flat out refused to do his job. He would not make us drinks on the menu with no explanation or alternatives as to which ones he could make. We had to go through a server to get a drink because he just didn’t want to do his job. When asked for water, we had to ask 4 times (4 different people came up from our group to ask) and waited over an hour for it. He seemed like he just wanted to be rude and useless for no reason and was some of the worst service we’ve ever had in the city. We truly would’ve been regulars if it wasn’t for the bartender being horrible.
Amazing pizza and amazing staff. Abbas is a man. Simply fabulous.
Abaz is the Goat he's kind and and funny. The pizza deserves Michelin star. BTW I'm 12

Artichoke Basille’s Pizza on MacDougal Street was a major letdown for us. We added it to our pizza crawl at my cousin Tony’s recommendation, but the signature artichoke slice just didn't work for me. It’s massive and a total belly buster; topped with a heavy, creamy sauce that tastes like spinach artichoke dip poured over dough. Knowing we had more stops on the crawl, I could only manage about a quarter of it.
​
On the plus side, the staff was very friendly and the service was excellent. Reviews in our group were split: Tony gave it a 10/10, but my wife and I landed at a 6.2/10. Worth a try if you love ultra-rich toppings, but for me, it’s a one-and-done.

Came around after 3pm. Buddy had a cheese slice. He liked it, but it was a little big for him. I had the crab slice. It was fine. It's passable. Crunchy crust. I'm sure a fresh out of the oven one would have been much better.
Excellent service, wonderful staff and excellent wine! Look forward to coming back!

Little Prince is always a great spot if you are lucky enough to get a table. Monday is usually a quieter night especially it you arrive at an off hour.
The place has remained charming and intimate over the years. If you want to gossip the next table will definitely hear you. Tonight we opted for sitting at the bar. The bartender was very attentive and made a great martini with perfect olives.
The menu is on the small side but enough to choose from. We shared the branzino, French onion burger and the ratatouille.
My friend preferred the burger and funny enough I liked the fish better. The fries were great, a little more on the done side with just a hint of salt. The ratatouille is prepared cubed style and alittle crunchy. I much rather the ingredients sliced so it's more of a softer medley.
Best to make reservations, especially if you are more than 2 people.

They tumbled from first to worst.. Seated our reservation for 2 After similar parties arriving later and then devoted their primary attention to an adolescent birthday party. With so many kids to take care of, with the food quality was mediocre too.

Very rude staff. Hostess scolded us to push our chair in (there is very little space in the restaurant) and then when we asked to move to a booth where we would have more room they lied and said they had a big party coming in so we couldn’t sit at the other table with more room. Meanwhile no one actually sat down at the table so the hostess completely lied to us. 1 star for dishonesty by the hostess who thought it was Ok to scold and lie to paying customers. Don’t go here, the NYC restaurant scene is too competitive to get treated like this by waitstaff and the food is mid.

Btw to everyone who is considering this restaurant- go look at all the 1 star reviews about the terrible service lol and don’t waste your time, clearly it’s not just us.

To start with the positive, we were in and out in under an hour. But to be honest, we did not feel the need to linger given the subpar food, atmosphere, and service. There is absolutely no notion of hospitality. The hostess lacks affect and has no business being in a service-facing field. We were asked repeatedly to move our seats closer into our tiny table, which was already crowded with out winter coat and bags. When we asked to move to a booth, the hostess refused insisting that there was a party coming in. None arrived in the entire hour we were there. The stuffy attitudes and loud music made a tiny space feel even smaller.

As for the food itself: except for the burger, the entire menu lacked the same finesse. I am currently nursing soda water and anti-acid trying to clean up the disaster that was the chicken dish. The menu says it's chicken, but if you close your eyes, you'll swear you're eating two breast-sized pieces of garlic. That was the only flavor which was odd because they promised salsa verde, which they said was actually an herb medley. I indeed saw the greens but I couldn't taste them or the chicken. Just garlic. Mountains and mountains of garlic.

The French soup was exciting at first bite but unfortunately disappointed thanks to the cheese atop which not bubbly, not golden, but subtly burnt as though it was sprinkled with cinders. The special ravioli was soaked in an orange lemon sauce that would have been more appropriate for vanilla ice cream. Cocktails were tiny, and the lemonade had an interesting lemon to sugar ratio: all sugar, a bit of lemon, and a rogue seed. Hey, at least it was made in house.

This restaurant is great if you don't really care for good tasting food and need somewhere to sit for no more than 60 minutes.

It was absolutely amazing! The dancers were so professional!

They were completely immersed in the music and dance.

My jaw was practically glued to the screen the whole time. We drank for two people, and it cost around $520.

Duane Park is one of the best nights out in NYC. The atmosphere is beautiful, intimate, and completely unique. The live band is incredible, the singers are phenomenal, and the performers are the most talented in the city. Every part of the show feels polished, exciting, and world class. An absolute must for a special night out in New York.

An unforgettable experience in New York. And that says a lot considering the incredible number of dining and entertainment options Manhattan has to offer.
This is a place where you can enjoy outstanding food while being immersed in a truly unique atmosphere. The menu is not large, but it changes regularly, which makes the experience feel fresh and special.
During my visit, I chose the pan-seared duck confit, braised beef short rib, and crème brûlée for dessert. I also tried the Espresso-A-Go-Go cocktail, which was excellent and a perfect way to start the evening. Every dish was beautifully presented, served at the right time, and absolutely delicious. The portions were generous enough to fully appreciate the flavors without feeling overwhelming.
What makes this place truly exceptional, however, is the atmosphere and the show itself. The organizers have managed to create an intimate and cozy setting in a relatively small space, making every guest feel like part of the performance rather than just a spectator.
The performers are incredibly talented, charismatic, and full of energy. Their connection with the audience is effortless, and that energy spreads throughout the room, creating a genuinely memorable experience.
The price is fixed and includes a cocktail, appetizer, main course, and dessert. It is certainly not inexpensive, but in my opinion, it is worth every cent considering the quality of both the food and the entertainment.
Overall, this was one of the most memorable evenings I have had in New York. If you enjoy great food, live performances, and unique experiences, I highly recommend adding this place to your list.
Such a nice place to catch up with friends over coffee. I enjoyed my visit and would love to explore more of the menu next time.
Bagel and cappuccino was so good, and the staff were so nice to my friend and I

Such a cool spot. The aesthetic is really unique and beautiful, and the whole place has a great vibe. The coffee was delicious—the s’mores latte in particular was fantastic. Friendly, welcoming service too. Definitely worth a stop in SoHo.
Waited 20 minutes for my carne asada burrito. Every single piece of beef was filled with fat and it was literally inedible  , could not even chew it
Very disappointing. Tortilla taste like a pancake. The meat is bland. Nothing else exciting going on.

I went pollo with guac and got the escabeche veg and the green dipping sauce. I manned up. Holy Mary mother of god. That was 10/10. 11/10. I have actually said out loud”that’s the best burrito I’ve ever had” It’s not my first rodeo. I promise you whatever I have tomorrow will have the rest of that green sauce on it. Formidable.
Cauliflower and potato burrito is gross. Bland with mushy texture.
The burrito fell apart in my hands when I took it out of the container. I asked them to re wrap it and they somehow did a worse job.
The breakfast burrito was very small and cost almost 18 dollars. I asked for hot sauce and they told me it was $2 extra. Super bland as well do not recommend
I ordered a burrito.  This is their burrito.  Not mujado.  The food that literally evolved so you could eat it with your hands on the go.
How can a place like this survive? Bad food bad service. I’ve never had a worse burrito in my life.

One of my favorite (affordable) omakase spots in NYC! There’s several locations!

The lineup is solid and the rice is always on spot. The fish always fresh. And the chef always super kind and attentive.

My night with my wife was especially special because we were the only ones there. Chef took extra special care to us and we enjoyed every single bite.

This place was founded on a quick(30 min slot) + affordable omakase which is what I loved. I’m a fast eater and love value so always come back to this spot. We weren’t rushed this time due to the lack of people there but we thoroughly enjoyed the omakase.

Pictured: a special piece by the chef with freshly caught lobster, caviar, gold leaf on Japanese milk bread.

Phenomenal experience! Chef Jen was so experienced and professional. The cuts of fish were so fresh especially the hamachi & hokkaido scallop! Ryan was our server and he was so kind and made our night! Would recommend 10/10

This place was killer…. The crispy rice is off the hook!  Was talked into it by Bill (sushi ninja) and it was amazing.   I would eat it daily!  The staff is top notch!  Why wasn’t there a line around the block?  You are crazy not to be blowing this place up… we were crazy lucky to just walk in without knowing anything about this place.   This sushi spot is a gem! Bill loves this food and is a wonderful guide through this taste experience!
Good food and ambiance!! There’s a cool bar setup in the back too

The name is 99 Cent Pizza. However, the cheapest slice costs $1.50.

It's only advertised that way; there's no indication that each topping costs extra. As soon as you order, the pizza goes into the oven, and you're asked to pay.

In the end, it costs almost $4.

It's pure rip-off, especially since there's no warning. Don't be fooled, folks.

Come here often for the cheap pizza. You really can’t beat their prices. Recently I came in and while waiting for my pizza I had a vertigo episode. The staff immediately took care of me and was so incredibly friendly and kind. 10/10 neighborhood pizza place ran by the nicest people with some of the best prices in the city if you’re looking to feed a lot of people for cheap.

Not bad actually. 4 slices of cheese pizza for $6. Nothing is really 99 cents but its ok,  all other pizza places around are much more expensive. Good taste and saves you from starving when you're on a low budget 😅

Incredible tuna melt! I love a spot that heats up the bread and cheese separately and then adds that to the tuna mixture, rather than heat up a tuna mixture in an oven with the bread. The crispy onions were the chefs kiss! Hope I get to try more sandwiches from here. So good! And great customer service.
