Deliciously refreshing tea, fast service, and in a relatively scenic location. Bit of a hole in the wall place, right across from the Basilica of St. Patrick's Old Cathedral... Take a moment to try this hidden gem out.
This was last year’s most hyped new restaurant.  Some super interesting and creative dishes but I wasnt blown away by the actual tastes of everything. Honestly I don’t think it’s worth the hype.

NY traditional high end French and adjacent dining scene is dying out. But if what replaces it is places like Ha's, I can't complain. I've tried the entire menu more than once, and not only there wasnt a bad dish, there wasn't an uninteresting one.

The place is distinctly casual, gritty and cramped. Probably not the best for, like, a traditional date night.

But I'd definitely recommend coming with a date (or a friend) because, if you're hungry enough, you can order the entire menu to share. Or maybe exclude one dish that might not be to everyone's taste. Beats just about every fancy "tasting menu" in New York

I had ordered buttermilk pancakes with strawberries. The pancakes were tasty but the strawberries on the plate were way too less compared to the portion of the pancakes. I would highly recommend adding more strawberries to balance the dish better.
The food is delicious. The breakfasts have very generous portions and excellent ingredients.

I used to visit the Sarabeth's in Tribeca, so I decided to try the newer Greenwich Village location. Although it's smaller, it's cozy, comfortable, and has a relaxed atmosphere. I was well received and the service was very good. The pancakes were just as delicious as I remembered, and the goat cheese omelet was perfectly prepared. It was a very enjoyable lunch, and I'll definitely be back the next time I'm in New York.

Sarabeth’s Greenwich Village was the perfect spot for breakfast. The food struck just the right balance between light and decadent, and everything was delicious. The welcoming setting and thoughtful service also helped make my daughter’s birthday especially memorable.
my favorite coffee shop of all time. xoxo love ENLYS og #1 fan.
Good coffee with various choices, we enjoyed it on a rainy day but way too expensive! Others shops around offer for less...

ENLY has become part of my daily routine, and I genuinely look forward to getting my strawberry shortcake matcha every day! 💗 It’s genuinely hands down the best matcha I’ve ever had and  I’ve tried so many places in NYC and LA. I even go out of my way to Soho just for ENLY! Aside from that one  experience, my visits have always been wonderful. The quality and taste keep me coming back, and ENLY will always be my favorite matcha spot! 💕 Thank you so much .

These drinks are seriously disgusting and overpriced. My friends got the iced banana latte which is literally blended banana and milk with the nastiest shot of espresso, I think the machine was dirty or the shot was burnt because it was truly horrible. One of my friends just threw his drink out which was around $10 and I asked for the other drink to be remade and explained what was wrong only for it to taste exactly the same. I got a chai with oat milk and it tasted like water, I'm not even exaggerating how bland it was, I couldn't even taste the oat milk at the very least. I'm assuming the other drinks may be worth a try but not for almost $15, there are plenty of better coffee shops in the area that dont have such a hostile environment and insane prices. I suggest taking your bad reviews into consideration for development, because I know there are more unvoiced negative opinions as everyone outside the cafe was disgusted and unsatisfied with their drinks.
Super fast and efficient for how busy they are. Superstars!

Great place! Everything is fresh and super tasty. Finally healthy and delicious food in New York!

I ordered a custom bowl to go, and when I got home, I realized several things were missing, including the extra chicken I paid for and the spicy sesame sauce. My bowl actually came with no sauce at all. For the price, it’s frustrating to not receive what I ordered, especially when I didn’t realize until I was already home. I really wanted to love this place, so I’m hoping this was just a one-off experience!
We ordered shawarma sandwiches; they were absolutely delicious! I highly recommend them. 👍🏻

Amazing selection and beautiful vibe with a cozy atmosphere. I recommend highly, and when you go, I promise you won’t be disappointed.

Great whisky selection.
Very cool experience

The individual behind the bar had no knowledge of the whiskey he served and couldn’t answer a single question our party asked him. We asked him 6 questions about whiskey ranging from what is your favorite US whiskey? What is your favorite scotch? What is your favorite brandy? What is your favorite bourbon. How about cognac? Irish whiskey? His response was “I don’t know” and he couldn’t elaborate any further nor did he care to. We spent over $300 for a couple of 1 oz pours. If you don’t know just pretend you do. We all know this whiskey is marked up to absolute ridiculous secondary prices and you are taking advantage of that. At least have some passion and knowledge of your business. Whiskey was great but the bartender could have been a lot better.

Copper & Oak is an absolute sanctuary for whiskey lovers right in the heart of the Lower East Side. If you appreciate a good pour, this place is a must-visit. The vibe is perfectly rustic and cozy dim lighting, exposed brick walls, and the rich, oaky scent of aged spirits hit you the moment you walk in. It feels like a hidden speakeasy dedicated entirely to the art of whiskey.

Best whisky bar I've experienced in the US. I'm a Scotch collector, I wasn't surprised to find all kind of allocated bourbons and ryes (Pappies, Russel's 13, Michter's 10, 20 and what not), but the real gems for me were the superb Scottish independent bottlings and the incredible knowledge of the very gracious bar keeper. Had a wonderful time.

I have gone to many sushi spots as well as omakases. This one stands out with the sushi, warm atmosphere and of course Chef Edgar who makes you feel like your in his home and couldn't be more welcoming. Can't wait to come back again soon.

Run to this one!!

My friends and I had the most amazing Omakase experience here. Everything was phenomenal - especially the uni. I think some of the best I’ve had and I am a foodie. Japanese melon at the end was also a nice touch and very delicious. This place is a must try in NYC - thank you chef Edgar!!!

Can’t wait to come back!

Chef Edgar was amazing and you can tell he was very proud of his ingredients. He was like a kid with all these toys that he wanted to show everyone. We bought a Groupon deal and ended up paying an extra $40pp upgrade to get a few extra courses and it was definitely worth it. Waiter said the Groupon deal didn't have uni so it was an easy decision to upgrade to get Hokkaido and Santa Barbara uni. We added on a tuna cheek nigiri which was the fattiest piece of and more uni at the end It was one of the best pieces of uni I've had and I regret not getting more. Everything just tasted amazing and I highly recommend it.

My husband and I just had lunch on Friday at Edo Ya with Chef Edgar, and wow, what an experience!

First, the ambiance is peaceful and beautiful--great way to have an omakase.

We originally got the 14-course, but ended up changing to the 19-course omakase halfway through because it was amazing!!

As others stated, he sources his fish directly from Japan and all tasted so incredibly fresh.  It started with appetizers including sashimi and lobster.

For the nigiri, the rice is seasoned where it has a little bit of a darker tint (which is usually a good sign that it'll be delicious!), a perfect flavor to accompany the fish.  He took the time to explain each piece of nigiri to us.  It'll always change due to what's available, but our favorites were the Santa Barbara uni, scallop (never had scallop like this before!), seared sole and seared toro collar!

This place ranks in the top omakase experiences we've had in NYC.  Will definitely be back!

What a beautiful and amazing place. Outstanding fish quality. We spent the night talking with the chef/owner who was serving us. This place needs to be in every food lovers address book. Can’t wait to go back
Perfect amount of food, fresh flavor and speed for lunch.  Cozy clean environment with thoughtful staff when I dine in. I pick this over any fast casual “pick your protein” place in Manhattan.
The naan was unfortunately quite flavorless and small. Tasted like it may have been frozen prior, which I hope is not the case? Disappointed by this spot.
Food was tasty
Stopped in the Essex st location on 10-25-2026 at 11;30 a.m. ordered the gotham smash with everyting plus a french fries and a coke.$23.76. Burger was too greasy for my liking. Live and learn.
Very tasty smash burger, felt like good value for money
One of the best indian restaurants ive been to in the city. Great flavor and excellent service.

Delicious, inventive fare at a reasonable price!!!

Food was fantastic and the entire team was incredibly welcoming. I highly recommend the Gobi Manchurian!
The food here is phenomenal, fresh, and flavorful. The owner Aman is a gracious and courteous person and the energy is reflected in the food and vibe of the place. 10000% recommend!

I visited The Highlight Room because It’s my friends birthday and I wanted to treat her to a good time. I kept seeing the space on social media and figured it would be a good time. But mid way through we were rushed to close our tabs and leave.

The location is beautiful and the drinks are a solid 8 out of 10. The server was nice.

But the experience as a whole felt very rushed. The moment we got our second round of drinks they asked us to close our tab. We were quite compared to the groups of people around us. The drinks were just placed on the table. And we still had food we were working on on our table. As women in the service industry this just felt rude and unacceptable. I made it clear to the server we felt this way and while I appreciate the half ass apology.
I wouldn’t recommend this space for anything beyond a golden hour drink before going elsewhere for dinner reservations.

waiter forgot about our food, there was no way to charge my phone, our server disappeared and we couldn’t get the check for about 30 minutes. When we finally went up to the bar ourselves to ask for the check, the bartender said he couldn’t help us, so we had to wait even longer until another server finally charged our card. Service is great every time. Probably my favorite rooftop in NYC for a good mix of a lounge/Club. Amanda was our VIP Server last time and was very attentive.

We visited on 10/17/26(Sat) - we walked in and chose the barstool seating by the window (this restaurant is walk-ins only). The staff is very attentive & friendly, and the food is delicious. Highly highly recommended - we will definitely visit again.
Immaculate vibes, everything you want in a wine bar.
Solid wine menu that’s interesting, staff is great haven’t tried the food yet but overall the vibe is fabulous.
Fun and intimate venue for live blues. I have my favorites but I've never seen a bad show. Reasonable cover.

Great place to hear blues music, great drinks and wonderful atmosphere.

Amazing place for blues, I'll repeat on my next visit. Totally recommend it.

Avoid this place at all cost, the space is dark as hell and the tables are so narrow with candles with fire. I burned my precious jacket and I witnessed one lady almost burned her hair. Lovely.

Every bureka I have tried has been amazing and the pickles and accompaniments have always been great. I am also excited to try the bubatons, they look great. The only reason why I am giving this a four and not a five is because I found the service to be noticeably not great. It's a mix of apathetic college students working there, who are a little slow at completing things and come off a little rude to the customers. They take their time plating stuff, are often just chatting with each other before completing something. I thought it was maybe going to be a one time thing, but every time I have gone in, it's been the same experience, which makes me think there's an odd work culture going on there. Highly suggest, but I would maybe save yourself the trouble of the bad service and order on Postmates.
The opening hours on Google Maps are incorrect. Waste of time...
Love the bingsu! The purple rice yogurt is also very good. Not too sweet

Absolutely love this place from trying it for the first time over the weekend. I wish I had taken pictures. Already missing it and wish that it exists where we live in MA. Definitely coming back next time coming to NY!!

Tasty veggie dumplings and Thai basil fried rice.

new favourite spot that i’ll be showing everybody! had the mango sticky rice vegan ice cream and some drinks, great atmosphere and super friendly service. we walked in and got a spot just after lunch. very attentive to allergies and intolerances
Outstanding in every since of the word. Food was perfectly flavored, portions were generous, and prices were so reasonable. This is a must try spot.

I needed a cup of Joe this morning, so I headed out and walked over to the Dunkin' located on West 3rd St. & Thompson St. This is my second time coming to this location since being in the city, and the reason I keep coming back is that the coffee tastes fresh and the customer service is wonderful. Each time I've been inside, they always greet me with a hello and a smile.
Today, I ordered my coffee and a seasonal pumpkin donut. Since I enjoyed my service so much the last time, I left a friendly tip for the gentleman working the register because he was just so polite to me. To my surprise, I found that he had left a second donut inside my bag! That was such a nice gesture of appreciation back toward me. He didn't have to leave me that second donut, but he did it anyway.
Who says New Yorkers are rude? From my experience, they are some of the kindest, hardest-working people around. So, if you're in the neighborhood, stop on by this Dunkin', grab a cup of Joe, and enjoy the pleasant atmosphere at this shop!
They are very welcoming and friendly.
Delicious wings and great prices!! Will definitely go back
Great staff and tasty food

Best fried chicken in the city. Had the garlic soy wings: crispy, juicy, meaty, & super flavorful. Coleslaw and pickled radish were also excellent. Service is prompt, efficient, and polite. The store is basic but they pack to-go wings well. Stayed hot and crisp on the subway. Will return.

As an Ethiopian food lover I’m picky about my injera, and this place has the perfect taste and texture.  The vegetarian combo was the highlight. Every dish had its own distinct flavor, and together they hit everything you want from Ethiopian food.

Would recommend for some tasty comfort Ethiopian. No frills, casual, Ethiopian restaurant.

36$ for one beer , over salty pancake and sauces.

Cathy provided excellent Service with a smile. l enjoyed the Tacos \
Great little cantina! Taco Tuesday is a great deal! Good tacos and 6 dollar beer can’t complain! Will be my spot over here. Really friendly staff

Omg we stumbled on a gem here!  Actually my son had already been here but we walked from a fashion show so we needed hydration and this was perfect because drinks were BOGO.  We each had 2 layovers and got slightly rocked.  Highly recommend the layover.
I want to come try the hh deal again. The frozen espresso martini with whipped cream is amazing
Awesome variety of sandwiches. Great taste fair price!
Exactly what it's supposed to be. Friendly, good Jewish salami option with the breakfast special. Reasonable prices.
Friendly neighborhood places like this are sometimes overrated on Google. Very organized, very friendly. Food is mediocre.

A very affordable and authentic diner where you can feel like a true American from the moment you walk in. Big plates of great food, refillable coffee—everything you could want from a diner. It's full of locals and far from the typical tourist spots, making the experience feel even more authentic. I would 100% recommend it if you're staying in NYC!

I’ve never had such a dry, flavorless turkey club. And it was twenty dollars. No drink or fries or anything. Twenty dollars. I can’t speak for the other food on the menu but good lord that sandwich may as well have been cardboard. I also asked for white bread and it came out wheat. A shame because they’re on my route home from work. Do yourselves a favor and go to Kassar’s up the street instead.

Came out to dinner with my best friends and had an absolute amazing time!!! Love Negril Village and big big shout out to Renae and Linden! Their personality, friendliness and service made the night that much better! I will looking forward to seeing them again when we come back!
From the food to the drinks, but more importantly our girl Renee that waited on us. She made our night. The food hit the spot. Thanks for the experience
Renae Linden was an amazing service!! This place never disappoints!!!

From start to finish, this spot is the bomb. A live DJ setting the mood. Awesome service from Jamie as a host and Rashida as a server. Jerk chicken Rasta pasta was so flavorful and the oxtail and grits were savory and creamy. Definitely returning on my next visit.
Had such an enjoyable and delicious brunch today.  Special place.
Loved this restaurant. We went here for dinner on our anniversary and the tasting menu was exquisite. Very nice staff and environment. We’ll be back for sure!

Not my cup of tea. Taking home this poor experience with me. Seating is limited. Service is very poor. Very understaffed for the crowd size.

great ice latte, friendly staff :))

I came to this location under no impression as i have never been here, I was blown away by the food i ordered and the service was amazing, Nima our server was very welcoming and persistent with her service, amazing server, great food, highly recommended! :)

It's pretty good! Not too much seating inside but it's got a good vibe. I got the chicken teriyaki bowl and my friend had a ramen. Someone on the staff is a reallllly big fan of 21 Savage and Drake though, which was fantastic. Haven't heard those songs in a hot minute. Would definitely recommend if you're in the LES.
Exceptional venue, great music, perfect ambiance. Cana was very welcoming.
Small place but music is good and dj is great. It’s a nightclub for people who want to be awake all night..!!

This is a night club for dancing House music. That’s it, and it works. Awesome sound system, music selection is not what you find on a music streaming service. The drinks are expensive for my budget but the ambience, music and sound system make it worth it. The bar guys could have a less primadona attitude, but overall good place. Ambience reminded me of Cielo. Get a pre-purchased ticket and you will save the line and bouncer’s mood. I would come back. Demi Riquisimo was a very good DJ.

Outstanding coffee and desserts. Great sit down spot too in an awesome location.
I've been here more times than I care to admit. The stuff here is really good. I particularly like the cupcakes and the key lime bar. You can taste all the little ingredients and it's very delicious.
Most mediocre carrot cake and someone stole my umbrella there!

I left annoyed and won’t be going back or recommending it to friends.

We came here on a Sunday afternoon and absolutely loved it!  Pairing wine with ice cream is such an elegant idea, and one that seems so obvious in hindsight that it’s hard to believe nobody thought of it sooner.  The pairings were delicious, and the whole experience was a really lovely way to spend an afternoon.  Highly recommend!

In today’s times, it’s very difficult to slow down, take a photo, have some incredible ice cream, and engage in wholesome conversations with friends. Do not miss the olive oil ice cream, its out of the world!
Such a fun concept I like unconventional parings and I appreciate that they created combos for you. A chill vibe

loveee the photobooth + ice cream and wine combo in this little hidden spot. the vanilla bean ice cream with olive oil and sea salt was absolutely delicious. photobooth is $12 for two strips. can’t wait to come back and try the wine pairing.

Had an excellent time. Food was fantastic, and the service was impeccable. I accidentally dropped my napkin. Without asking and within a minute, I had a new one. And that's just one example..

There was hair in both dishes I had.. towards the end of service while there were still many people around us, one lady (who wasn’t our waiter) came up to our table and immediately said “are you guys ready??” And then rolled her eyes when we told her she could take some plates.

The carbonara was salty and some bits of the pork in my dish was so hard I had to spit it out.

Cheese and honey pairing were phenomenal.
Delicious food and great service. The focaccia and meatballs are the best.

Second time here after having a subpar experience years ago. This visit was phenomenal - everything was perfect and delicious from start to finish.

Recs - focaccia (soft and doughy) and prosciutto, tuna crudo, radicchio salad, amatriciana, cacio e pepe, tiramisu, mango sorbet (not sure if this is on the regular menu but they brought it out for my birthday and it was incredible).

My hubby and I are staying here because of work in our apartment. It's location is just 2 blocks from us, which is very convenient.  Room service is every day. And free breakfast.

It's confirmed that all of the locations are pretty small in scale, I've always assumed the Manhattan location to be bigger than it actually is, but I was able to find seating considering I may have been the 1st one to the spot, which was also a drawback as well because not all of their specialty pizzas were ready yet. Very small place. The pizza was okay, nothing special. I probably wouldn't go again.
Omg I fell in luv with the chef 🥺 I wish you all nothing but abundance and prosperity. Food on a thousand 🥰🫵🏽💯💪🫡
this slice was sooooooo good omg im still thinking about it weeks later

Excellent Thai spot, nice and small but the food I top tier. Got a rice box w/ chicken broccoli and mushrooms and a pad see yew w/ tofu. I hope the consistency stays the same because the food is so damn good.

Friendly staff- husband and wife run the shop they very sweet -foods was great I got the chicken and pineapple fry rice it was very tasty just perfect amount of seasoning- it was fresh made by order not many seats has 4 seats small cozy spot I will return to try other things on the menu please support small business

Very friendly professionals and the food is iconic and tasty!

EVERYTIME we travel to New York from Delaware, we make sure to stop by here! Never been disappointed. Today we had pepperoni pizza slices, vegetable slice and a chicken/bacon with ranch. Can't wait till our next visit.
Best pizza ever!!!!!!!

Great place for a quick and good Peruvian food experience, I go a few times a week since its conveniently located inside Essex Market, I always get my food for take out so fast, and take it to the sitting area or take it home to enjoy it, this Peruvian food experience is trending lately all over the world. Too bad they don’t sell alcohol like at the main location otherwise, I’d be enjoying a drink while waiting for me food. Prices are so low that I can’t let this opportunity pass, you definitely got to try it.

The food is good, but in my opinion, the portions could be more generous.
The space is a bit small, but I appreciated the efficient service from the cashier and the kitchen staff.

I came across this place through a post by Resilentos, and honestly, Don Ceviche is the best… great atmosphere, fantastic service, the kitchen team outdid themselves with some delicious ceviches, and especially the guy at the register who had the patience of a saint because I was undecided and he even gave me great advice… I'll definitely be back next time and always!

I would suggest that the owners look into serving from bigger bowls that wouldn’t challenge physics as much.

Price is expensive, close to $20 for a kakigori, but this seems to be the norm in NYC so it’s nothing too outrageous.
my favorite kakigōri spot in nyc!!

Definitely worth a visit, one can only say it's great!

Delicious iced oat latte. The espresso was strong, with just the right amount of oat milk. So many cafés drown out the espresso with too much milk, but this was perfectly balanced. Will definitely return.
Tiramisu is too heavy but super cute
Delicious food with generous portions. My girlfriend and I both enjoyed everything that we ordered. Thank you for the good service!
The food is A1 and affordable. Great calm, relaxing environment with very friendly service.
Excellent Drunken Noodles!! And a cute reataurant!
Friendly and quick service. Drinks look very fun and fairly priced. I got the fried banana dessert and it was very yummy.

Cafe Grumpy on the Lower East side is a quiant, atmospheric, and fun coffee shop. It smells so aromatic the minute you walk thru the door. I had a delicious and rich hot chocolate. The server's artistry topped off my beverage with a beautiful design in the froth.

Booking: Excellent. Friendly, accommodating, and consistently gracious with reservation changes. A standard befitting a high-end restaurant.

Food: The biggest disappointment. Two dishes feature “9” in their names, yet one is a turkey, lettuce, and tomato sandwich and the other a burger. At this price point, both the execution and culinary ambition fall short of expectations. The tuna tartare was a decent exception.

Atmosphere: A beautiful space, complemented by an enjoyable live performance. Unfortunately, the collective chatter makes conversation difficult, undermining the intimate, inviting atmosphere suggested by the restaurant’s photographs. Acoustic design would make a meaningful difference.

Service: Warm and attentive throughout. However, visibly unclean glasses are a small but telling lapse in a restaurant aspiring to this level.

Price: Approximately $200 for two, including tax and tip, for a shareable starter, two entrées, wine, and a cocktail (no dessert).

Verdict: A missed opportunity. The space has all the ingredients to become one of New York’s standout dining destinations, but the food and finer details do not yet match its promise. With greater culinary ambition and attention to execution, this could be a very different experience. For now, I wouldn’t return.

I celebrated my birthday at Estela, a one Michelin starred restaurant tucked away in a small, cozy space. I had high expectations coming in, but unfortunately, most of the dishes left me feeling underwhelmed.

They started us off with sourdough bread and olives, and surprisingly, the bread was one of my favorite things of the night. Fresh and warm, with a crunchy crust and a soft, doughy interior. Simple but so good.

Endive Salad: The highlight of the meal! Probably the second best salad I’ve ever had in my life. Served with walnuts, anchovies, and citrus juice, the combination was perfectly balanced and packed with flavor. I could honestly come back just for this. A MUST order!

Fried Arroz Negro: Essentially squid ink fried rice, but there was barely any squid, if any at all. The dish felt underwhelming and was missing the seafood element I was hoping for.

Ricotta Dumplings: Pretty good overall, served with thinly sliced mushrooms. Nothing mind blowing, but a solid dish.

Golden Tilefish: Unfortunately, this was dry and overcooked, very disappointing.

Pork Collar: Another disappointment. The pork was noticeably undercooked, and the dish fell short in both execution and flavor.

The portions are on the smaller side, almost like tapas, so the bill adds up quickly without feeling particularly satisfying. I really wanted to love Estela, especially given its Michelin star and reputation, but aside from the endive salad and sourdough bread, the meal didn’t leave much of an impression.

If you’re looking for top-quality dim sum that delivers on flavor, texture, and value, this place absolutely deserves a visit! Every dish we tried had something special about it, and the quality of the food really stood out.

The soft, pillowy roll paired with that rich, sweet, creamy egg filling was absolutely incredible. I could have easily ordered more of these alone!

And the sweet sesame balls? Absolutely TOP NOTCH! Some of the best sesame balls I’ve had, hands down. That perfect texture and delicious sweetness made them an excellent way to finish off the meal.

What really impressed me was how reasonable the prices were. For food of this quality, the value is fantastic. You get dishes that deliver on flavor without feeling like you’re breaking the bank. The service was fair — nothing extraordinary, but it got the job done.

Overall, this is easily one of the better dim sum restaurants I’ve been to! Great food, fantastic flavors, crispy textures done right, incredible desserts, and prices that make you want to come back and try even more of the menu. This place absolutely delivered, and I’ll definitely be back to explore more of what they have to offer. If you love dim sum, this one is worth checking out! 🥟🔥

Hidden behind a discreet facade in the heart of SoHo, Rei Restaurant offers an intimate 20-seat omakase-style counter where Japanese tradition meets modern culinary art. 🕯️✨

Our 7-course seasonal Kaiseki journey unfolded seamlessly: 🍵 Starter: Velvety, mirror-smooth Crab Chawanmushi followed by pristine, delicately sliced seasonal sashimi with a cool, clean finish. 🥢 Simmered:Tender cabbage leaves wrapped around rich Wagyu absorbing a deep, savory dashi, or slow-braised beef tongue that melts effortlessly on the tongue. 🔥 Fried: Chutoro Tatsuta-age—lightly marinated medium-fatty tuna flash-fried to a crisp exterior while keeping the center luxuriously semi-raw and buttery. 🍚 Rice: Nagoya-style Unagi Hitsumabushi, finished tableside with savory sweet glaze and later transformed into a comforting ochazuke broth. 👑 Main: An extravagant harmony of hand-cut Wagyu Yukke, plump sweet uni, and briny caviar that pops delightfully on the palate. 🍵 Dessert: A refined Monaka trio layering crisp wafer shells with smooth red bean/chestnut paste, rich chocolate, and chewy mochi.

A quiet, meditative masterpiece from start to finish. 🥢💫
Amazing, recommended!

I learned before my visit that kaiseki is all about culinary art. The whole meal unfolds step by step, focusing on ingredient quality, plating and dining atmosphere.
At Rei in SOHO, you can tell the chef puts a lot of thought into every dish. The plating and presentation are thoughtful, and every course is visually pleasing.

Kaiseki is inherently a refined dining style with smaller portions, meant to be savored slowly.
One small regret: my English isn’t fluent enough to have an in-depth chat with the chef about ingredient selection and the ideas behind each dish.

Great for anyone who enjoys slow dining and appreciates culinary aesthetics. If you’re looking for a filling meal or great value for money, you may want to adjust your expectations.

*Rei might be the best restaurant in Manhattan.*

Absolutely one of the WORST dining experiences I have had in a very long time, if not ever. We came in and sat quickly- table for 4. We ordered pasta, a Caesar salad, nachos with chicken, a burger and the steak burger. The pasta and salad came out FIRST, mind you that was food for two people. Those two people had to begin eating their food to keep it from going cold, waiting on the nachos (which is a friggin’ appetizer btw!) and the two burgers. Absolutely ridiculous. People come out for dinner to eat TOGETHER. They finished their entire meals while we still waited well beyond that for our food. Mind you, we started with a bottle of water being brought to the table- NO GLASSES to drink from!!! The soft drinks are bottled and FLAT, no fizz, ZERO flavor. We ordered bar drinks which took AGES to come, meanwhile the bartender is on her PHONE, while customers WAIT!!! When the nachos and burgers did come, they were COLD… BARELY even flipping ROOM TEMP!!!! So you mean to tell me, we waited nearly 40 minutes for the food to be delivered cold?!! I literally could not believe this dining experience.

If you’ve had high tea before this will be underwhelming. If you haven’t, it’s cute. It’s also $50 a person so really the price for what you get is fine. We did high tea. The tea was nice, the sandwiches were not very good. The bread was stale. I think they must have made the tea sandwiches and left them exposed to air. I know they must prep in advance but if the kitchen would wrap them in a slightly damp paper towel you can avoid the bread drying out. The scones were not good at all. The jam was huge lumps of preserved strawberries. Not at all what it’s supposed to be. Our server was lovely. The place is quite small and cramped. We had a 4pm reservation and had to wait for people to finish which wasn’t ideal as there’s not much space to wait. Overall for the price it’s fine but it’s not a true high tea. This is more a place for instagram content and young people that don’t know what a real high tea is.

Visited on September 8th

Casino is a beautifully sexy and elegant restaurant, perfectly situated in a pocket of the Lower East Side where time feels delightfully suspended. It sits in one of the few corners of Manhattan that hasn't been homogenized by rapid gentrification. Here, the true spirit of New York's melting pot remains entirely intact. Looking out, you witness a vibrant crossroads of cultures--a rich diversity that is beautifully mirrored in both the neighborhood's people and the exceptional variety of its culinary landscape.

This was my second visit to Casino, and I was eager to return after being blown away by the food, service, and decor the first time. On this second visit, it felt like walking into an entirely different world--in the best way possible. The dining room transported us straight into a 1940s movie, offering a smoky, sexy, and elegant ambiance (minus the actual smoke). My husband and I were celebrating our wedding anniversary, and the team perfectly set the mood by accommodating our request for a red banquette. Our waitress was incredibly warm, friendly, and offered excellent recommendations. When I asked for wine pairings, she seamlessly transitioned us to Daniel, the sommelier. His recommendations were absolutely beautiful, pairing flawlessly with both my appetizer and entree. My only slight disappointment was that he sent our waitress over to pour and sample the wine rather than presenting it himself.  He did drop by at the end of our meal but it was bittersweet.

My husband and I had a mixed culinary experience here, marked by some disappointing appetizers but truly exceptional pasta dishes.

The Grilled Prawns with Calabrian Chili: We were both pretty underwhelmed by this dish. It lacked the vibrant punch we were expecting.  The Funghi Fritti (Tempura Battered Mushrooms): Honestly, these were awful. They were literally rock-hard, and no amount of lemon aioli or Calabrian chili sauce was going to rehydrate them. The Main Courses: Bucatini with Clams: My husband opted for this and thought it was delicious. The sauce was absolutely gorgeous; his only minor critique was that he wished there had been a bit more of it.  I ordered the Tagliatelle Bolognese: This was the absolute star of the night. It was, without a doubt, the best Bolognese I have ever had in my life.

We highly recommend this hidden gem!

P.S. The hostess checked on every table except ours.

The ribeye was very tender and flavorful, served with grilled onions, peppers, and baby corn, but at $60 it didn’t feel like a particularly good value. The standout of the meal was actually the ice cream served with the donuts—it was outstanding, both in flavor and texture, and may have been some of the best ice cream I’ve ever had. The PUBLIC hotel is incredible, I believe it truly caters to all needs. We stayed in Queen Hi-Floor rooms which were a perfect size for a six night trip.

I especially want to mention Lasandra, Jonathan, and both reception teams who were there on the evening of the 15th and morning of the 16th. I wouldn't have been able to navigate such a difficult situation without their help and I will be forever grateful they were there.

On the note of your staff, I also had the pleasure of meeting Ella and Solana, in both the rooftop bar and the downstairs bar behind the pool table. They were so hospitable, and such lovely girls!! Unfortunately I had the unpleasant experience of running into quite a rude and aggressive patron of the downstairs bar, behind the pool table. From what I could understand this man was not a guest of the hotel and was being incredibly rude to bar tender on duty that night and her bar back (I didn't catch their names). I complained about this behaviour to the bar manager that night, I believe their name is Jay and said I would like this person removed for being so disgustingly rude to their staff there, of which Jay refused to do. I understand situations like that need to be handled carefully, however from my own observations I could tell the staff behind the bar that night were uncomfortable with this man and I believe Jay did not look out for his staff appropriately and this should be addressed internally.

Overall, my family and I had the most incredible time in NYC and our stay at The PUBLIC hotel was everything we had hoped for and more.

We will be returning.

Kindest, Stella

**Heavy on style, light on amenities**

Everything at the Public screams "Design," and some of it is genuinely good. Our corner loft room was spacious, with a beautiful exposed concrete ceiling and dramatic views. But the yellow, semi-transparent glass toilet enclosure offered little privacy, and closet space was tight for one of the largest room categories. There's no room service, no turndown service, no coffee machine and no minibar, just a small, empty fridge.

The WeWork-style lobby is open to the public and packed with laptop-wielding hipsters, leaving little or no room for hotel guests, and there's nowhere else to lounge. The cocktail bar was closed for two of our four days. That left the rooftop bar, which is pleasant, weather permitting, if you can ignore the sour staff.

There's no real restaurant either, just a ground-floor deli and breakfast bar with equally unhappy staff. The continental breakfast included in the rate is meager: drip coffee or tea, orange or grapefruit juice, and one item such as a croissant. Sandwiches are extra. At an average of around $800 a night, you'd think they could throw in a cappuccino, or keep their dignity and not include breakfast at all.

Most of the time there is only one person at the reception desk, which means long queues. This was at its worst when we came back for the luggage we'd left with the hotel after checking out. The unfriendly receptionist told us no one was available to fetch bags from the luggage room and that we'd have to do it ourselves. So six groups of guests trooped up to the second floor to find an office she'd pointed us to, where someone could finally take us to the luggage room.

If you're willing to spend $800 a night, there are far better hotels in New York that offer the same design fix but know a great deal more about amenities and customer service than the Public.

I don’t recommend booking this hotel if you’re traveling with anyone else! The staff is wonderful and the hotel is clean, but the bathrooms are designed with a transparent coating so you can see the figure of whoever is showering or using the toilet from anywhere in the room. Without a proper door, it makes the whole thing a little too intimate of an experience with a companion.

My stay at PUBLIC Hotel left a lot to be desired, starting with a frustrating check-in experience. Despite arriving at 3:10 PM (past the 3:00 PM check-in time), I was unable to use the iPad check-in because I hadn't received a room number yet.

When I spoke to the front desk, I was told my room wasn’t ready because the previous guest had a late check-out, and that my personal request for robes and slippers—which I had submitted three weeks in advance—was causing an additional delay.

When I asked for an ETA, I was simply told to come back in 20 minutes. I returned around 3:30pm and spoke with another staff member who gave a vague answer. Given the inconvenient delay that nearly made me late for an uptown reservation at 5pm, I asked if a late check-out could be accommodated for my departure day. I was told they couldn't approve it at the desk and I’d have to call down later. No gesture or accommodation was offered to alleviate the inconvenience, making for a poor first impression.

To top it off, when I finally got to the room, the robes and slippers I requested three weeks prior were missing. When I asked about them later that evening, I was told they were completely out of slippers, though we did eventually receive the robes.

On a positive note, the room itself was clean. However, noise traveled easily through the door and you could hear people talking in the hall, making it less than peaceful.

Ultimately, I’ve had much better service and hospitality at other New York City hotels, and unfortunately, I will not be returning.

I attended an event here tonight and was accused of stealing FREE merchandise.
When I walked in, a friendly staff member at the name tag table encouraged me and other attendees to check out the stickers at the table perpendicular to hers. I watched several people ahead of me take merchandise from that table, and when it was my turn, I did the same. I want to emphasize this was FREE merchandise — just like the food and matcha drinks being handed out elsewhere at the event, which nobody else was questioned about.
As I zipped up my bag, a staff member approached me and said, "I was not allowed to put that in my bag." I was confused and asked, "You mean the FREE gear we were just told we could take?" He replied, "I have to go check in to see if YOU can have that."
I was understandably offended. I had just watched other people take the same items, and I'd been explicitly told it was for everyone. I waited while he went to "verify" something that had already been made clear. He came back and confirmed, with total confidence, what I already knew.
What made it worse: I recognized this same staff member from earlier, stationed by the door. When another guest in line asked him why there were two lines, he said he didn't know and pointed down the block to someone else as the "point person."
Being singled out and accused like this put a real damper on an event I'd been looking forward to. I'm not writing this review because I was mistaken for a moment — I'm writing it because instead of a simple apology, he doubled down and made me feel like I was in the wrong. In hindsight, I should've escalated it on the spot, but the staff already looked overwhelmed managing the line, and I didn't want to make a scene over stickers.
I enjoyed the rest of the event and didn't let his weaponized incompetence ruin my night. But I won't be back ,  my loss, I guess.

I liked the room, which is annoying in retrospect. It was small, a little cramped, and full of the kind of references I grew up around in family restaurants. For a minute it felt quaint, familiar, like somebody’s actual kitchen. The meal did not survive that impression.

We had come for the fusion, that New York meeting of Hispanic and Chinese food, which is hardly a wild idea in this city. You would think someone in the building could talk about it. The waitress could not. Questions got hesitant, flummoxed half-answers, with no opinion and no sense of what was worth ordering. She set the plates down and left. Water was not refilled. A premade iced tea and a straw took about ten minutes. We were in the back booth by the bathroom, along one narrow walkway, so there was nowhere for her to pretend she was not passing us. She did, ten or twelve times, without a word, clearly clocking whether we were done. In a room that small, a stare is not subtle. The attention arrived for the exit and never for the meal. It felt scrutinized, and a little discriminatory.

The portions were generous for the price, and that is the only credit I will give. The food was greasy, overcooked, and mushy, oversalted and still underseasoned, with a gamey edge that belonged to neither tradition. The broccoli beside the sesame chicken was the best thing on the table, which is a miserable thing to have to admit. Everything else tasted like a five-minute search for the dish it was supposed to be. A bastardization. The drinks were the same failure in a glass: too tart and sour, or so sweet the fruit had disappeared.

I can speak for the Chinese side. The people with me can speak for the Hispanic side. None of us took this as gospel, and none of us were impressed. This city already has rooms that love both cuisines, and rooms that fuse them without embarrassing either one. This was the neighborhood worn as a costume. An overrated cash grab, with none of the love and none of the craft. I would not go back.
